DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The clinical picture of sudden vertigo lasting only three minutes, triggered by movement, with no auditory symptoms, neurological deficits, or systemic risk factors is classic for BPPV. Since your episode has resolved, the next step is a physical bedside exam, such as the Dix-Hallpike maneuver, to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected canal.
